text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — High error rate observed on /v1/generate (service: inference-service). Spike started ~1768004300. Possible KV/prefix cache inconsistency. Paging on-call: @alice (primary).

alice: taking this. joining now. any immediate customer impact? :eyes:

carla: seeing 500s from runtime for a subset of requests. stack: serving-runtime -> prefix-cache -> model. Errors look like 'kv-deserialize-failed' on some prefixes.

bob: adding logs: high ratio of cache hits turning into downstream decode errors. looks correlated with a concurrent deployment to cache-populator yesterday.

alice: tl;dr: if prefix cache returns corrupted entries, we return malformed logits -> 500s. mitigation options: 1) bypass prefix/KV cache for affected model family, 2) global rate-cap to reduce volume and give time to rollback, 3) route heavy tenants to fallback model. doing quick impact assessment.

dave: customers with active sessions: tenant-omega (~12% traffic), tenant-delta (~3%), rest small. tenant-omega sees ~30% error rate on generation calls.

eva: notif draft to customers is ready, but want to confirm mitigation first. we should avoid large blast if reduced to specific tenants.

alice: immediate actions I will attempt now:
- flip feature flag to bypass prefix cache for model 'rw/fastgen-v3' on prod
- apply per-tenant rate limit for tenant-omega (rps 5) at edge
- add traffic-shaping to send 20% of tenant-omega traffic to fallback model 'rw/fastgen-v3-quant' (known-good path)

alice: running flag toggle (will paste command):
```
# disable prefix cache for fastgen-v3 in prod
curl -X POST https://ops-console.internal/api/flags \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"prefix_cache.enabled","scope":"model:rw/fastgen-v3","value":false}'
```

sre-bot: deploy-bot report: flag-change queued to 3 clusters. estimated propagation 30-90s.

carla: while that propagates, I'll apply the edge rate-limit for tenant-omega.

carla: envoyctl config update:
```
route:
  match: host:api.redwood.ai tenant: tenant-omega
  rate_limit: requests_per_second: 5
```

sre-bot: rate-limit applied to 2/3 frontends, remaining will sync in 40s.

bob: started traffic-shaping job, 20% -> rw/fastgen-v3-quant. Pin rollout id: ts-17680045. Command:
```
rtcast route update --tenant tenant-omega --split 80:rw/fastgen-v3,20:rw/fastgen-v3-quant
```

alice: monitoring metrics. error rate for tenant-omega dropping from 30% -> 10% within first 2 mins. overall 500s still elevated but falling.

dave: note: disabling prefix cache increases token compute, watch latency SLO. dashboards show p50 latency up ~40ms, p95 up ~150ms for the model.

alice: acknowledged. current mitigation plan: keep cache bypass + tenant rate-limit + 20% traffic to fallback. That should buy us time to rollback bad cache population job or scrub corrupted keys.

bob: on the rollback: suspect bad populator run id: pop-2026-03-14T03Z. Carla, can you isolate the run and roll back? If not, we should evict KV keys for affected model namespace.

carla: isolating now. if rollback not possible fast, I can run a targeted prefix eviction: `kvctl evict --prefix rw:fastgen-v3:prefix:* --dry-run` then remove.

alice: please hold on eviction until we confirm safe window; eviction will cause more cold misses. fine to evict a narrow set of corrupted prefixes once identified.

eva: customer comms: sending to tenant-omega now: short status + mitigation + ETA for full resolution ~2-4h. cc'ing account team. draft:
"We're seeing generation errors; we've throttled traffic and enabled fallback routes while we investigate. Some increased latency expected. Working on a fix — we'll update within 1 hour."

incident-bot: incident severity set to SEV2. paging rotations notified: alice (primary) -> bob (secondary) -> dave (next)

alice: let's capture runbook steps for postmortem: owner: alice, rollback owner: carla, infra vet: bob, comms: eva. ETA: attempt to identify corrupted keys and scrub, or rollback populator run.

sre-bot: alert: CPU on serving nodes increased by 18% after cache bypass. autoscale group responding; might hit capacity if sustained.

alice: keep autoscale on. if capacity becomes a concern we will throttle more aggressively. Carla, if eviction is required, prefer targeted eviction for prefixes with 'deserialize-failure' tag.

carla: got a list of ~120 keys with deserialize errors from logs. preparing a targeted eviction list. Will run a small batch now (10 keys) as canary.

carla: running canary eviction: `kvctl evict --key rw:fastgen-v3:prefix:AB12CD34` -> success.

alice: monitoring error counts. good — error rate dropped further to 3% on canary. Proceed with batched eviction of remaining flagged keys in groups of 50 with 2 min observation windows.

bob: started batched eviction. also started scrub job to validate payload checksums for remaining keys.

dave: ops note — keep support pages updated: add a banner for 'generation degraded, mitigation active'.

eva: customer update sent. responses: some tenants see latency but accept mitigation. one high-touch customer asked for SLA credit; escalating to account team.

alice: final state for now: prefix cache bypass remains on for rw/fastgen-v3, tenant-omega rate-limited to 5 rps, 20% of tenant-omega routed to fallback. Eviction completed for flagged keys. Error rate back to baseline ~0.2%.

alice: preparing handoff. shifting paging to bob for the evening. Handoff summary:
- root cause: corrupted KV/prefix entries (likely from populator run pop-2026-03-14T03Z)
- mitigations applied: prefix cache bypass (model-scoped), tenant rate-limit, traffic-shape to fallback, targeted kv eviction
- impact: tenant-omega had increased 500s and latency; now stable. compute up due to cache bypass.
- follow-ups: scrub remaining keys, patch populator to checksum writes, run postmortem, update runbook for quick eviction procedure.

bob: taking over. I'll watch overnight and coordinate rollback if scrub finds more corruption. posting runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-corruption

alice: thanks team. leaving channel to handoff. :white_check_mark:

bob: acknowledged. I'll keep the flag bypass for 4h then evaluate revert. If stability holds, we can re-enable prefix cache after verification.

incident-bot: incident updated: status -> monitoring. incident closed to active responders at 1768009121. Postmortem owner: alice.
